docs.title: Helix SSPA Controller
docs.text:
Control and protection for solid-state HF amplifiers. The controller pairs an STM32G474 control board with an ESP32-P4 touch display, switches bands automatically from your radio, and trips in hardware on SWR, filter reflection, temperature and current.

Pick your hardware revision in the tabs on each page. This manual matches firmware [x.y]; use the version menu at the top to read an older one.

RF safety

High RF power. Never operate without a proper load or antenna connected.

docs.title: System overview
docs.text:
The controller sits at the centre of the amplifier: it switches the RF path, biases the pallet, watches SWR, temperature, voltage and current, and talks to the radio, the display and the optional modules. Numbered blocks are explained in the notes on the diagram.

System block diagram. Click to enlarge, or [download the PDF](assets/wiring/helixrf-sspa-v4-block-diagram.pdf) for printing.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
The short path from a wired controller to a working amplifier. Each step links to the full instructions.

RF safety

High RF power. Never operate without a proper load or antenna connected.

  1. Wire it up. Follow Connectors and wiring. Power up on 12 V only, with the 52 V supply off, and check that the display starts.
  2. Set the current sensor. Choose the sensor type in the High Side Switch's power module settings (shunt, Hall or BTS) and enter its values.
  3. Set the LPF map. Tell the controller which LPF bank each band uses.
  4. Set the temperature sensors. Enter each NTC's resistance and beta, and the fan low and fan high temperatures.
  5. Set the protection trip levels. On the protection page, adjust the trimmers for voltage, current and temperature.
  6. Choose the band data source (band voltage, BCD, CAT, CI-V or RF sense) and your radio profile.
  7. Calibrate power and SWR, then test every protection trip into a dummy load before going on the air.

See Setup and calibration for each step in detail.

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
Wire the modules to the controller as shown in Connectors and wiring. It has the system diagrams, and a pin-out and wiring sketch for every connector.

Suggested order:

  1. 12 V supply (J22) and the display (J18).
  2. High Side Switch: sense (J8) and control (J10).
  3. LPF module: power (J39) and band select (J43 or J41).
  4. SWR bridges (J3, J5), NTCs (J28) and fan (J20).
  5. PTT and RX/TX relay (J26), PA bias (J30).
  6. Radio band data (J1 or J16), ALC (J24), and the optional antenna selector and rotator.

Connectors and wiring →

docs.title: Connectors and wiring
docs.text:
Every connector on the controller board, what it does, its pin-out and how to wire it. Pin numbers follow the board silkscreen; pin 1 is GND on almost every connector.

RF safety

High RF power. Never operate without a proper load or antenna connected.

Two footprints per connector

Most connectors appear twice on the board under two reference numbers, for example J3 / J4. The first is a JST PH (2.0 mm) side-entry socket, the second is a row of solder pads wired in parallel. Use whichever suits your build: a crimped JST PH lead, or wires soldered straight to the pads. Never use both at once.

docs.title: J22 / J23 · 12 V power in
docs.text:
The 12 V logic supply for the controller, the display, the fan and all relay outputs. It is fused on the board (F1, resettable).

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 +12 V In [TODO: input range and current needed with all relays on] 
 12 V supply                       Controller J22
 ┌─────────┐                       ┌──────────┐
 │    +12V ├───────────────────────┤ 2  +12V  │
 │     GND ├───────────────────────┤ 1  GND   │
 └─────────┘                       └──────────┘

Warning

The 52 V PA supply never goes to the controller board. It runs through the High Side Switch module (see Power diagram).

docs.text:
Supplies 12 V to the LPF relay board. Two pins per rail share the current.

Pin Signal Direction 1, 2 GND 3, 4 +12 V Out

docs.title: J8 / J9 · PSU monitor
docs.text:
Voltage and current readings from the High Side Switch module, shown on the display and used by the protection. Pin 4 powers the sensor.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 V_SENSE In PA supply voltage, scaled by the module 3 I_SENSE In PA current: shunt amplifier, Hall sensor or BTS current-sense output 4 +3.3 V Out Supply for the sensor

The sensor type (shunt, Hall or BTS) and its values are set on the display. See Setup and calibration.

 Controller J8                      High Side Switch (sense)
 ┌───────────────┐                 ┌─────────────────┐
 │ 4  +3.3V      ├─────────────────┤ sensor supply   │
 │ 3  I_SENSE    │◄────────────────┤ current out     │
 │ 2  V_SENSE    │◄────────────────┤ voltage out     │
 │ 1  GND        ├─────────────────┤ GND             │
 └───────────────┘                 └─────────────────┘

docs.title: J10 / J11 · PSU protection
docs.text:
Turns the 52 V PA supply off when the hardware protection latches a fault. Both polarities are provided, so the switch module can use whichever its gate driver needs.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 ~PROT-VCC Out Fault output, inverted sense 3 PROT-VCC Out Fault output 4 +3.3 V Out Supply for the switch logic

[TODO: state the active level of each pin (switched to GND on fault?) and which one the HelixRF High Side Switch uses.]

 Controller J10                     High Side Switch (control)
 ┌───────────────┐                 ┌─────────────────┐
 │ 4  +3.3V      ├─────────────────┤ logic supply    │
 │ 3  PROT-VCC   ├────────────────►│ enable / kill   │
 │ 2  ~PROT-VCC  ├────────────────►│ (use one)       │
 │ 1  GND        ├─────────────────┤ GND             │
 └───────────────┘                 └─────────────────┘

docs.title: J30 / J31 · PA bias
docs.text:
Switches the pallet's gate bias. The controller applies bias only while transmitting, after the RX/TX relay has settled (20 ms), and removes it before the relay returns to receive. A protection fault removes it at once.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 BIAS-IN In Bias supply from the pallet 3 BIAS-OUT Out Switched bias back to the pallet's gate-bias input 4 Gate kill (optional) Out Pulls the gate to GND on a fault 5 +12 V Out Supply for an external pinch-off circuit 6 −12 V Out Supply for an external pinch-off circuit 7 PINCH Out Protection-latch signal for a pinch-off circuit 8 BIAS_CTRL Out Logic high while transmitting, for pallets with a bias-enable input

Most LDMOS pallets need only pins 1–3. Pins 4–8 are for pallets that need a hard gate kill, a negative pinch-off voltage or a separate bias-enable signal. [TODO: wiring notes for the pallets you support.]

 Controller J30                     RF pallet
 ┌───────────────┐                 ┌──────────────────┐
 │ 2  BIAS-IN    │◄────────────────┤ bias supply out  │
 │ 3  BIAS-OUT   ├────────────────►│ gate bias in     │
 │ 4  Gate kill  ├ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─►│ gate (optional)  │
 │ 8  BIAS_CTRL  ├ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─ ─►│ bias enable (opt)│
 │ 1  GND        ├─────────────────┤ GND              │
 └───────────────┘                 └──────────────────┘
       ─── required    ─ ─ optional

docs.title: J3 / J4 and J5 / J6 · SWR bridges
docs.text:
DC outputs from the two directional couplers. J3 / J4 reads the bridge on the antenna side (after the LPF). J5 / J6 reads the bridge between the PA and the LPF, which catches a wrong or failed filter. Both feed the power meter and the hardware SWR trip.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 Reflected (ANT-R / LPF-R) In DC from the reflected detector 3 GND 4 Forward (ANT-F / LPF-F) In DC from the forward detector

Use shielded cable or a twisted pair per signal, and keep it away from the PA output coax.

 SWR bridge                         Controller J3 (antenna) / J5 (LPF)
 ┌──────────────┐                  ┌──────────────┐
 │ FWD detector ├─────────────────►│ 4  FWD       │
 │          GND ├──────────────────┤ 3  GND       │
 │ REF detector ├─────────────────►│ 2  REF       │
 │          GND ├──────────────────┤ 1  GND       │
 └──────────────┘                  └──────────────┘

Calibrate both bridges after wiring; see Power calibration.

docs.title: J28 / J29 · NTC temperature sensors
docs.text:
Two NTC thermistors, for example one on the pallet heatsink and one on the LPF or the PSU. The fan speed and the over-temperature trip follow whichever reads higher. Each NTC sits between +3.3 V and its sense pin; the board has a 10 kΩ resistor from each sense pin to GND.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 +3.3 V Out NTC 1 supply 2 NTC-1 In NTC 1 sense 3 +3.3 V Out NTC 2 supply 4 NTC-2 In NTC 2 sense

Use 10 kΩ NTCs [TODO: confirm recommended NTC value and beta]. Enter each NTC's resistance and beta on the display.

 Controller J28
 ┌──────────────┐        NTC 1 (heatsink)
 │ 1  +3.3V     ├────────/\/\/\────┐
 │ 2  NTC-1     ├──────────────────┘
 │              │        NTC 2
 │ 3  +3.3V     ├────────/\/\/\────┐
 │ 4  NTC-2     ├──────────────────┘
 └──────────────┘

docs.title: J20 / J21 · Fan
docs.text:
Variable fan speed. The speed ramps from 10 % at the "fan low" temperature to 100 % at "fan high"; the fan never stops completely. Two-wire fans are switched on their negative lead; four-wire PC fans take the PWM signal.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 PWM Out PWM control for 4-wire fans 3 FAN − Out Switched negative for 2-wire fans 4 +12 V Out Fan supply (filtered) 2-wire fan4-wire PC fan 
 Controller J20                 Fan
 ┌──────────────┐              ┌──────────┐
 │ 4  +12V      ├──────────────┤ + (red)  │
 │ 3  FAN −     ├──────────────┤ − (black)│
 └──────────────┘              └──────────┘

 Controller J20                 Fan
 ┌──────────────┐              ┌──────────────┐
 │ 4  +12V      ├──────────────┤ +12V (yellow)│
 │ 1  GND       ├──────────────┤ GND  (black) │
 │ 2  PWM       ├──────────────┤ PWM  (blue)  │
 └──────────────┘              └──────────────┘
   (tach wire not used)

If the fan runs backwards to the temperature (fast when cold), turn on PWM invert on the display.

As above.

docs.title: J41 / J42 and J43 / J44 · LPF band select
docs.text:
Eight band outputs to the LPF relay board, one per filter bank. Exactly one output is on at a time. Which bank each band uses is set in the LPF map on the display. The outputs are given twice, so you can use whichever matches your relay board:

  • J43 / J44 (LPF): sourcing. The active pin goes to +12 V. Wire each relay coil between the pin and GND.
  • J41 / J42 (~LPF): sinking. The active pin goes to GND (open collector). Wire each relay coil between +12 V and the pin.
Pin J43 / J44 (sourcing) J41 / J42 (sinking) 1 BAND1 ~BAND1 2 BAND2 ~BAND2 3 BAND3 ~BAND3 4 BAND4 ~BAND4 5 BAND5 ~BAND5 6 BAND6 ~BAND6 7 BAND7 ~BAND7 8 BAND8 ~BAND8

[TODO: maximum current per output.]

Sourcing (J43)Sinking (J41) 
 Controller J43                 LPF module (one bank shown)
 ┌──────────────┐              ┌────────────────────────┐
 │ 1  BAND1     ├─────────────►│ relay coil ──┐         │
 │ …            │              │              GND       │
 │ 8  BAND8     ├─────────────►│ (one per bank)         │
 └──────────────┘              └────────────────────────┘
 Power the LPF board from J39 (+12 V and GND).

 Controller J41                 LPF module (one bank shown)
 ┌──────────────┐              ┌────────────────────────┐
 │ 1  ~BAND1    ├──────────────┤ relay coil ── +12V     │
 │ …            │              │                        │
 │ 8  ~BAND8    ├──────────────┤ (one per bank)         │
 └──────────────┘              └────────────────────────┘
 Relay +12 V comes from J39.

docs.title: J45 / J46 · Antenna selector
docs.text:
Drives the optional 4-way antenna selector and a separate receive-antenna relay. All outputs are sourcing (+12 V when on). The TX antenna is chosen per band on the display and never changes while transmitting.

Pin Signal Notes 1 ANT1 TX antenna relay 1 2 ANT2 TX antenna relay 2 3 ANT3 TX antenna relay 3 4 ANT4 Dedicated RX antenna relay 5–8 EX1–EX4 Spare outputs [TODO: describe use]

The TX antenna relays use a cumulative code, so a cascade of three changeover relays selects four antennas:

Antenna ANT1 ANT2 ANT3 ANT 1 (default, no relay on) off off off ANT 2 on off off ANT 3 on on off ANT 4 on on on 
 Controller J45                     Antenna selector board
 ┌──────────────┐                  ┌─────────────────────────┐
 │ 1  ANT1      ├─────────────────►│ K1 coil ─┐              │
 │ 2  ANT2      ├─────────────────►│ K2 coil ─┤  coils to    │
 │ 3  ANT3      ├─────────────────►│ K3 coil ─┤  GND         │
 │ 4  ANT4 (RX) ├─────────────────►│ RX relay─┘              │
 └──────────────┘                  └─────────────────────────┘

[TODO: GND and +12 V for the selector board. J45 has no GND pin; take GND from the chassis or J39.]

docs.title: J26 / J27 · PTT and RX/TX relay
docs.text:
Keying input from the radio and the drive for the RX/TX changeover relay. The controller sequences the relay and the bias so the relay never switches with RF present.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 ~PTT In Active low: radio's TX-GND / SEND output pulls it to GND 3 nRST-RLY Out Switched to GND (open drain) [TODO: describe use] 4 RX/TX RLY Out +12 V while transmitting; flyback diode on board 
 Radio                Controller J26              RX/TX relay
 ┌──────────┐        ┌──────────────┐            ┌──────────┐
 │ SEND/PTT ├───────►│ 2  ~PTT      │            │          │
 │      GND ├────────┤ 1  GND       ├────────────┤ coil −   │
 └──────────┘        │ 4  RX/TX RLY ├───────────►│ coil +   │
                     └──────────────┘            └──────────┘

Test before going on the air

Check that the relay changes over on PTT with no RF applied, before you connect the drive cable.

docs.title: J24 / J25 · ALC and TX inhibit
docs.text:
ALC feedback to the radio, and a TX-inhibit line that stops the radio from transmitting while a protection fault is latched.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 ALC (4 V range) Out [TODO: confirm range and polarity] 3 ALC (10 V range) Out [TODO: confirm range and polarity] 4 TX-INH Out Switched to GND (open drain) on a fault

Use the ALC pin that matches your radio's ALC input range.

 Controller J24                     Radio
 ┌──────────────┐                  ┌───────────────┐
 │ 2 or 3  ALC  ├─────────────────►│ ALC in        │
 │ 4  TX-INH    ├─────────────────►│ TX inhibit in │
 │ 1  GND       ├──────────────────┤ GND           │
 └──────────────┘                  └───────────────┘

docs.title: J16 / J17 · CAT / CI-V
docs.text:
Serial link to the radio for automatic band switching by CAT (two-wire serial) or Icom CI-V (single wire). Logic level is 5 V or 3.3 V, set by solder jumper JP2. Pin 4 powers a level converter (RS-232 or USB) if you use one.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 CAT-RX In Data from the radio 3 CAT-TX Out Data to the radio; the CI-V line in CI-V mode [TODO: confirm] 4 +5 V Out Supply for the CAT module CAT (TTL)Icom CI-V 
 Radio / CAT module             Controller J16
 ┌───────────────┐             ┌──────────────┐
 │ TXD           ├────────────►│ 2  CAT-RX    │
 │ RXD           │◄────────────┤ 3  CAT-TX    │
 │ GND           ├─────────────┤ 1  GND       │
 └───────────────┘             └──────────────┘

 Radio (CI-V jack)              Controller J16
 ┌───────────────┐             ┌──────────────┐
 │ tip (CI-V)    ├─────────────┤ 3  CAT-TX    │
 │ sleeve (GND)  ├─────────────┤ 1  GND       │
 └───────────────┘             └──────────────┘

Warning

Most radios' RS-232 ports use ±12 V levels. Do not connect them directly: use a level converter powered from pin 4.

docs.title: J18 / J19 · Display
docs.text:
Power and the serial link to the ESP32-P4 touch display. The display also passes firmware updates to the controller over this link.

Pin Signal Direction Notes 1 GND 2 RX In 3.3 V UART, from display TX 3 TX Out 3.3 V UART, to display RX 4 +5 V Out Display supply 
 Controller J18                     Display
 ┌──────────────┐                  ┌──────────────┐
 │ 4  +5V       ├─────────────────►│ +5V          │
 │ 3  TX        ├─────────────────►│ RX           │
 │ 2  RX        │◄─────────────────┤ TX           │
 │ 1  GND       ├──────────────────┤ GND          │
 └──────────────┘                  └──────────────┘

The display's own CAN port connects to the PSU CAN connector, where fitted (see the "Other I/O" diagram).

docs.title: J32 / J33 · Rotator
docs.text:
Antenna rotator control: two relay outputs and the position potentiometer. Supports 360° and 450° rotators with 3-point calibration.

docs.text:
Hardware comparators trip on high SWR, filter reflection, over-temperature and over-current, and a latch holds the fault. The default SWR trip is 3:1.
